title: HumanLLM: Towards Personalized Understanding and Simulation of Human Nature

problem.claim: LLMs often lack nuanced understanding of human cognition and behavior, limiting their effectiveness in social simulation and personalized applications.

gap.claim: Standard LLM pretraining on vast, uncontextualized web data does not capture the continuous, situated context of an individual's decisions, thoughts, and behaviors over time.

contributions.claim: HumanLLM is a foundation model designed for personalized understanding and simulation of individuals.
The Cognitive Genome Dataset is a large-scale corpus curated from real-world user data on Reddit, Twitter, Blogger, and Amazon.
The work formulates diverse learning tasks and uses supervised fine-tuning to predict individualized human behaviors, thoughts, and experiences.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The data pipeline automatically extracts over 5.5 million user logs through data filtering, synthesis, and quality control.
The authors report that HumanLLM outperforms base models in predicting user actions and inner thoughts, mimicking writing styles and preferences, and generating user profiles.
The authors report significant gains on out-of-domain social intelligence benchmarks.

narrative_sequence.summary: Interest in using LLMs to simulate human behavior is growing because of their progress on objective tasks.
LLMs have limited nuanced understanding of human cognition and behavior.
The stated cause is misalignment between uncontextualized pretraining data and individuals' continuous situated contexts.
The work introduces HumanLLM, constructs the Cognitive Genome Dataset, and applies task formulation with supervised fine-tuning.
The authors report improved individualized prediction, style and preference matching, profile generation, out-of-domain social intelligence, and applications in human-centric AI systems.

unknowns: The abstract does not report dataset composition, privacy protections, or user-log distribution.
